title: Have a Conversation
coreMove: Practice delivery until the talk sounds like one person speaking clearly to one person.
sourcePressure: The source says conversational delivery comes after conviction and story shape. It is built through practice, verbal control, and congruent body language: rate, volume, pitch, pauses, gestures, movement, recording review, and hands out of pockets.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says sound casual or wing it. The useful version says rehearse enough that naturalness survives pressure.

hook: imagine the audience is one friend
counterintuition: body language matters more than words

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a planner explaining a rezoning map to residents who expect jargon
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the room hears a human explanation or a bureaucratic recital
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she marks three places in the script where she will look up, lower the pitch, and speak directly to the front row instead of reading the parcel codes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded zoning map with yellow tabs sticking from the edges

exampleSpecs.audience: a resident leading a five-minute handoff practice for exhausted interns
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a safety script sounds usable at 3 a.m. or like training theater
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he rehearses the opening until he can say the checklist like a nurse at the bedrail, then removes the stiff training voice
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated handoff card clipped to a blue scrub pocket
mustAvoid: safety checklist as chapter two story

exampleSpecs.audience: a junior analyst presenting loan-loss exposure to senior partners
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the partners trust her judgment or hear a memorized spreadsheet tour
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she watches a rehearsal video, catches her hands trapped in her jacket pockets, and rewrites the first minute as a spoken briefing with one clean gesture to the risk column
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paused rehearsal video showing both hands buried in a navy jacket

exampleSpecs.audience: a friend officiating a ceremony for the first time
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the couple feels seen or trapped inside a polished script
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he practices the vows aloud until he can lift his eyes on the couple's names and let the pause land without rushing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: thin ceremony pages fluttering in a garden breeze

exampleSpecs.audience: a wildfire analyst addressing cabin owners before a dry summer
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether technical risk maps become a calm, credible conversation before evacuation season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks which slope will burn fastest, waits through the guesses, then practices the reveal so the silence after the map does not feel accidental
exampleSpecs.firstImage: red contour lines spreading across a laminated fire map

exampleSpecs.audience: a dean welcoming first-generation students and parents
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the opening feels institutional or like a direct welcome to anxious families
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you watch him replace the grand auditorium voice with a rehearsed first-row sentence, then use volume only after the welcome has landed personally
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a microphone stand centered under a banner of college crests

skillTargets: distinguish conversational delivery from casual improvisation
choose rehearsal moves for rate, volume, pitch, and pauses
evaluate whether practice has made delivery more human or more stiff

tryThisNowSpec: Record the first 45 seconds of a live talk, then mark one place to pause, one sentence to lower, and one gesture to remove before rehearsing it once more.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
